limitations: Jobs-only observer and sanitizer are not a complete preflight replacement; PTY pagination, separate stream registry and opaque native/facade dispatch/freeze remain false/HOLD.
No production observation or real-server end-to-end behavior was tested; transport calls mocked and standard HTTP parser exercised over in-memory bytes.
Deadline checkpoints bound socket operation timeouts and prohibit new submissions after expiry; cannot forcibly kill already in-flight system calls or prove exact OS scheduling latency.
JSON decoding, hashing and bounded CPU work have checkpoints around them, not preemptive interruption; filesystem open/stat calls are not forcibly interrupted.
FD metadata and before/after membership equality are observational checks, not an atomic transaction or a security boundary against arbitrary same-UID writers.
Matching request host plus native job_id supplies logical host association only; missing authority/nonce/supervisor flags remain false/None and do not grant terminal action authority.
publication_incidents: Four full large text writes returned INVALID_ARGUMENT Cannot write entire staging file; root verified no public destinations. A later explicit new attempt used <=16KiB create/append parts with each cumulative SHA verified. Unknown staging artifacts were not deleted.
An initial nonabsolute python3 executable was refused by argument validation before launch; /usr/bin/python3 with the same idempotency key then launched the authorized owned fixture.
The first six-file upload bundle exceeded capture budget before any file publication; it was replaced by per-file bounded capture.
